chunks: And Ali ibn Ahmad informed us, saying: Obaydillah ibn Musa al-Alawi informed us, from Ali ibn Isma'il al-Ash'ari, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:

You will be tested, O Shia of the Family of Muhammad, with the testing of kohl in the eye. And the owner of the eye knows when the kohl is put into his eye but does not know when it comes out of it. And likewise, a man may be upon our doctrine in the morning and have recanted it by evening, or be upon our doctrine in the evening and have recanted it by morning.

key_terms.شِيعَةَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Shia of the Family of Muhammad

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the kohl metaphor in the hadith about Shia testing during the occultation?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir employs the metaphor of kohl (*kuhl*) to illustrate the rigorous testing (*tamhis*) of the Shia during the Minor and Major Occultation. Just as one knows when kohl is applied but not when it falls out, believers may appear steadfast in the morning but have secretly recanted by evening, highlighting the uncertainty and hidden nature of true faith during times of trial. This imagery underscores the scholarly concept of *khafa'* (hiddenness) in religious commitment, where outward adherence may mask inner fluctuation, a key theme in Nu'mani's discussion of sectarian divergence.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (12) Ali bin Ahmad narrated from Obaydillah bin Musa al-Alawi from Ali bin Issma’eel al-Ash’ari from Hammad bin Eessa from Ibraheem bin Umar al-Yamani from someone that Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) had said:

“O Shia of Muhammad’s progeny, you are going to be tested like the kohl in the eye. One knows when the kohl is put into his eye but he does not know when it gets out of it. Just in the same way that one believes in our matter in the morning and recants it in the evening or he believes in it in the evening and when morning comes he recants it.”
